evidence: mobile-native/androidApp/src/main/java/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/navigation/Navigation.kt:490-495 — the Screen.CreateListing composable wires `onSubmit = { _ -> Result.failure(NotImplementedError("Wire to listing API")) }`. Every tap of the Publish button in CreateListingScreen unconditionally returns a NotImplementedError; the screen then shows either the 'network' or 'publish failed' banner via CreateListingScreen.kt:120-125. UC-51.4 (Realtor: publish a new listing) is not functionally deliverable in the Android app.

The entry point is reachable in production: MyListingsScreen exposes a 'Create' button wired to `navController.navigate(Screen.CreateListing.route)` (Navigation.kt:484), and the CreateListingScreen scaffold + form fields + Publish CTA are all rendered without any feature-gate or 'coming soon' state. A signed-in realtor can navigate to it directly from the realtor dashboard.

The KMP shared surface has no matching backend call: `grep -rn 'createListing\|CreateListing' mobile-native/shared` returns zero hits, and PortalListingsRepository.kt exposes only listMyListings + getListingAnalytics + getPortfolioAnalytics — there is no POST /api/v1/listings method to wire the callback to. Fix requires (a) adding `suspend fun createListing(input: CreateListingRequest): Result<PortalListing>` to PortalListingsRepository against the reality-server `POST` route, (b) mapping the composable's CreateListingInput to the wire request, and (c) replacing the NotImplementedError lambda with a real dispatch. Until then the CreateListing route should be feature-flagged off or the button hidden.

Systemic `!!` non-null assertions on nullable UI-state properties across the Compose androidApp: ListingDetailScreen.kt:121,125,132,149,160 (`state.errorMessage!!`, `state.listing!!` from `viewModel.state.collectAsState()`); InquiriesScreen.kt:169 (`errorMessage!!` from a local `var by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }`); FavoritesScreen.kt:164 (same pattern); AccountScreen.kt:174 (`notificationPrefs!!` inside `if (notificationsExpanded && notificationPrefs != null)`). Kotlin cannot smart-cast a property getter on `state` nor a delegated `var`, so the branch guard does not imply non-null at the use site.

The pattern is a latent crash class: while Compose's snapshot system usually keeps reads within one composition consistent, any state update between the null-check condition evaluation and the argument-list evaluation (e.g. the ViewModel's StateFlow emitting from a coroutine mid-composition, or a `LaunchedEffect` in a sibling branch mutating the local `errorMessage` state) will throw KotlinNullPointerException. This is the exact category of bug that killed VoteDetailScreen (see the neighbour segment's 2026-08-23 finding on Rules of Hooks) — silent-until-it-crashes state-management fragility.

Idiomatic fix mirrors how the same file already gates other branches: capture the value into a local val at the top of the `when` branch, e.g. `state.listing != null -> { val listing = state.listing; ... ListingContent(listing = listing, ...) }` or use `state.listing?.let { listing -> ... } ?: return`. The FavoritesScreen retry lambda demonstrates the safer style with `.fold(onSuccess = { ... })`. Applying the fix removes the `!!` and lets the compiler enforce the invariant.
